title: Architect tone anchors and interaction-ink refresh for dense toolbars and tables
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Refresh core semantic tokens and interaction ink for high-density surfaces (toolbars, tables, compact controls). This ticket scopes palette anchoring, a conservative typography uplift for small headings, a compact spacing/radius variant, and a multilevel micro-elevation stack to improve perceived depth while maintaining WCAG AA contrast. Goal: reduce visual noise in dense UIs, improve tap affordance on small controls, and provide a straightforward migration path for components and product teams.
acceptance_criteria: A stable token set (semantic names) published in the design token repo and console token preview
Compact density tokens (spacing/radius) available as token aliases and CSS variables
Interaction ink updated across primary/secondary/icon buttons with explicit opacity ramps for light/dark modes
Micro-elevation stack implemented and validated in Storybook with visual regression baselines
Migration guide + codemod PR opened and linked; at least one product area (data tables) migrated in canary
Accessibility checks: all foreground/background pairs meet WCAG AA for text and 3:1 contrast for non-text controls where required
design_notes: Anchor color strategy: introduce neutral-800 as primary surface anchor for dense components to reduce perceived saturation when multiple accents are present
Introduce accent-anchoring tokens: accent-ink (interactive highlights), accent-stroke (borders), and accent-bg-subtle for small pill states
Interaction ink: use layer-aware ink that combines alpha keying with elevated contrast; ink opacity ramps: hover 0.06, pressed 0.12 on light surfaces; hover 0.10, pressed 0.18 on dark surfaces

Typography: add compact headings (h6-compact) with -2px size delta from standard h6 and 0.05 tighter letter-spacing for legibility at small sizes; adopt variable font axis for optical size when available
Spacing/radius: introduce density.scale.compact (values: 4, 8, 12) and radius.small (4px) + radius.xsmall (2px) for chip-like controls

Shadows/elevation: move to a 3-layer micro-elevation: ambient (soft, 2px blur), penumbra (directional, 3px offset), and core (tight 1px outline). Combine layers into tokens elevation.micro-1/2/3 with clear z-index guidance
Token naming guidance: prefer semantic tokens (e.g., surface-toolbar, text-compact-muted, focus-ring-strong) and avoid component-specific names to ease reuse
engineering_notes: Runtime: console CSS variables must support both default and density.compact variants. Plan: --rwd-radius-xs / --rwd-spacing-compact-1 etc
Backward compatibility: provide a shim layer mapping old tokens to new semantic tokens for one release cycle. Codemod will rewrite: color.neutral-700 -> surface-toolbar where appropriate
Storybook: add a density knob and visual diff snapshots for toolbar/table stories. Reference PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/2146
Performance: ensure new shadow stack uses CSS-layered shadows (single property) where possible to avoid layout repaint overhead on hover
Rollout: canary in product 'analytics-dash' for 2 weeks, collect CSS metric for styling regressions and user feedback via in-app survey link
QA: unit tests for token resolution, E2E screenshot tests for compact toolbar and table row hover/active states
migration_plan: Phase 1 (Design): finalize semantic token map and publish token spec doc: Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-token-spec
Phase 2 (Engineering): implement CSS variables and Storybook examples; open codemod PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/codemods/pull/48
Phase 3 (Canary): migrate analytics-dash toolbar and data-table components to compact tokens; observe metrics and a11y reports
Phase 4 (Rollout): ship token aliases in minor release; announce deprecation of legacy component tokens with 2-release window
Phase 5 (Cleanup): remove legacy token fallbacks after deprecation window and update migration docs
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: small typography changes may reduce legibility for older users. Mitigation: run targeted a11y tests at 14px and 12px body scales and keep full-sized tokens as default
Risk: visual regressions in third-party embedded dashboards. Mitigation: provide fallback tokens and update CDN-hosted token CSS with opt-in flag until migration completes
Risk: contrast regressions when combining accent-ink with low-elevation surfaces. Mitigation: add lint rule in design tokens CI to enforce min contrast thresholds for token combos
